The choice depends primarily on mileage and ownership horizon . ✅ Choose REPAIR if: • Failure caught early (chain rattling but no damage, head gasket seepage only) • Vehicle worth £2,000-£5,000 • Mileage under 80,000 • You are selling within 12 months • Failure is truly isolated (sensor, minor gasket, single injector) • You are on a tight budget Default: Repair if failure is early and vehicle under 80k miles. ✅ Choose RECONDITIONED if: • High mileage (100k+) - timing chain, turbo, injectors, oil pump near end-of-life • Multiple failures present (chain + turbo + injectors) • Keeping car 2+ years • Vehicle worth £5,000-£15,000 • Catastrophic failure (seized engine, snapped chain with head damage) • Repair history indicates a pattern of issues Default: Reconditioned if vehicle has 100k+ miles and you plan to keep it 2+ years. Reconditioned engine replacement costs £1,800-£5,500 fitted, addressing all wear points. Repair is cheaper upfront but carries higher long-term risk on high-mileage engines. When should I repair rather than replace my engine- + Choose repair if: the failure is caught early (chain rattling but no damage, head gasket seepage only), vehicle worth £2,000-£5,000, mileage under 80,000, you're selling within 12 months, or the failure is truly isolated (sensor, minor gasket, single injector). When should I choose a reconditioned engine over a repair- + Choose reconditioned if: high mileage (100k+) - timing chain, turbo, injectors, oil pump all near end-of-life; multiple failures present; keeping car 2+ years; vehicle worth £5,000-£15,000; catastrophic failure; or repair history indicates a pattern of issues. What's the mileage threshold for reconditioned over repair- + The single biggest predictor of reconditioned choice is mileage . At 100k+ miles , the cumulative wear across timing components, turbo, injectors, and oil pump makes targeted repair a short-term fix. At under 80k miles , repair is usually the better choice. What are the hidden costs of repairing a high-mileage engine- + Common hidden costs: turbo failure within 12 months (£800-£2,500), injector failure (£300-£1,500), oil pump failure (£1,500-£3,000+ rebuild), timing chain tensioner failure (£650-£1,800), and labour overlaps from paying twice (£500-£1,500 wasted). Does a reconditioned engine eliminate future failure risk- + A reconditioned engine addresses all wear points: bearings, pistons/rings, gaskets/seals, timing components, oil pump, injectors, and turbocharger are all inspected and replaced if worn. This eliminates the cumulative failure risk of a high-mileage engine. What warranty comes with a repair vs reconditioned engine- + Repair: 3-12 months warranty on the repair only. Reconditioned: 12-24 months warranty on the whole engine. Always verify warranty terms with your chosen supplier. How long does a repair take vs a reconditioned replacement- + Repair: vehicle off-road 1-3 days . Reconditioned replacement: vehicle off-road 3-7 days (including sourcing, delivery, and fitting). Is a reconditioned engine worth it for a car worth £3,000- + For a vehicle worth £3,000 with under 80k miles and early failure - repair is usually the better choice. For a vehicle worth £3,000 with 100k+ miles and multiple failures - reconditioned cost may exceed vehicle value; consider repair or scrap. What if I'm planning to keep my car for 5+ years- + If you're keeping the car for 2+ years and it has high mileage (100k+), reconditioned is strongly recommended . It eliminates future failure risk and provides 12-24 months warranty, making it the better value decision for long-term ownership. faqs.answer: Choose reconditioned if: high mileage (100k+) - timing chain, turbo, injectors, oil pump all near end-of-life; multiple failures present; keeping car 2+ years; vehicle worth £5,000-£15,000; catastrophic failure; or repair history indicates a pattern of issues.

faqs.question: What's the mileage threshold for reconditioned over repair- +
faqs.answer: The single biggest predictor of reconditioned choice is mileage . At 100k+ miles , the cumulative wear across timing components, turbo, injectors, and oil pump makes targeted repair a short-term fix. At under 80k miles , repair is usually the better choice.

faqs.question: What are the hidden costs of repairing a high-mileage engine- +
faqs.answer: Common hidden costs: turbo failure within 12 months (£800-£2,500), injector failure (£300-£1,500), oil pump failure (£1,500-£3,000+ rebuild), timing chain tensioner failure (£650-£1,800), and labour overlaps from paying twice (£500-£1,500 wasted).

faqs.question: Does a reconditioned engine eliminate future failure risk- +
faqs.answer: A reconditioned engine addresses all wear points: bearings, pistons/rings, gaskets/seals, timing components, oil pump, injectors, and turbocharger are all inspected and replaced if worn. This eliminates the cumulative failure risk of a high-mileage engine.

faqs.question: What warranty comes with a repair vs reconditioned engine- +
faqs.answer: Repair: 3-12 months warranty on the repair only. Reconditioned: 12-24 months warranty on the whole engine. Always verify warranty terms with your chosen supplier.

faqs.question: How long does a repair take vs a reconditioned replacement- +
faqs.answer: Repair: vehicle off-road 1-3 days . Reconditioned replacement: vehicle off-road 3-7 days (including sourcing, delivery, and fitting).

faqs.question: Is a reconditioned engine worth it for a car worth £3,000- +
faqs.answer: For a vehicle worth £3,000 with under 80k miles and early failure - repair is usually the better choice. For a vehicle worth £3,000 with 100k+ miles and multiple failures - reconditioned cost may exceed vehicle value; consider repair or scrap.

faqs.question: What if I'm planning to keep my car for 5+ years- +
faqs.answer: If you're keeping the car for 2+ years and it has high mileage (100k+), reconditioned is strongly recommended . It eliminates future failure risk and provides 12-24 months warranty, making it the better value decision for long-term ownership.
